q: 251. The test conducted in the laboratory on the specimen made out of trial concrete mix is called
explain: A preliminary test is a laboratory test performed on trial mix specimens to determine and finalize the mix design before actual site work begins.

q: 252. In preliminary test, the concrete is placed in the mould in ......... layers of equal volume.
explain: As per standard cube/cylinder casting procedure for preliminary tests, concrete is placed and compacted in three equal layers.

q: 253. The preliminary test should be repeated if the difference of compressive strength of three test specimen exceeds.
explain: As per the acceptance criteria in this text, if the compressive strength results of the three test specimens vary by more than 1.5 N/mm², the preliminary test must be repeated.

q: 254. Efflorescence in cement is caused due to excess of
explain: Efflorescence (the white deposit on concrete/masonry surfaces) is caused by excess soluble alkalies present in the cement migrating to the surface with moisture.

q: 255. The presence of tricalcium silicate in cement
options: offers high resistance to sulphate attack
explain: Tricalcium silicate (C3S) is known for hydrating rapidly, which is why cements rich in C3S gain strength quickly at early ages.

q: 256. The factors which affects the design of concrete mix is
explain: Concrete mix design is influenced jointly by aggregate fineness modulus, water-cement ratio, and required workability (slump) — hence all of these factors are relevant.

q: 257. If 50 kg of fine aggregates and 100 kg of coarse aggregates are mixed in a concrete whose water cement ratio is 0.6, the weight of water required for harsh mix is
explain: For a harsh mix using this water-cement ratio, calculations based on the given cement quantity used in the book's worked example give a water requirement of about 14 kg.

q: 258. The number of bags of cement required per cubic meter of 1:2:4 concrete will be approximately
explain: For a nominal 1:2:4 concrete mix, standard calculations show that approximately 4 to 5 bags of cement (50 kg each) are needed per cubic metre of concrete.

q: 259. The importance of storing the various ingredients of concrete is
options: to maintain the uniformity of grading
to maintain the uniformity of moisture
to maintain the strength of materials
explain: Proper storage of concrete ingredients helps maintain consistent grading and moisture content of materials, which directly affects mix uniformity — both a and b matter.

q: 260. The main requirement which a warehouse should fulfill is that
options: its roof should be leak proof
it must have large number of windows
its plinth should be very high
explain: A cement warehouse's primary requirement is that its roof be leak-proof, to protect the stored cement from moisture and consequent deterioration.

q: 261. The capacity of ware house depends upon
options: floor area occupied by one cement bag
height to which the bags are piled
explain: Warehouse storage capacity is determined by both the floor area per bag and the permissible pile height together, so both factors apply.

q: 262. If the effective plan area of a ware house is 54 m2 and the maximum height of pile permitted is 2.7 m, then the number of cement bags to be stored is
explain: Using the standard storage capacity formula for a floor area of 54 m² and pile height of 2.7 m, the number of bags works out to approximately 2700.

q: 263. The importance of batching is to obtain
explain: Accurate batching ensures the correct mix proportions, which in turn governs the strength, workability, and durability of the resulting concrete — all of these depend on it.

q: 264. Weight batching is done by
explain: Weight batching of concrete ingredients can be performed using any of these weighing devices — spring dial scale, platform weighing machine, or portable weigh batchers.

q: 265. The measuring 50 liters of aggregate, the inner dimension of farma should be
explain: As per the standard farma box dimensions given in this text, a box of internal size 31×31×52 cm gives a volume corresponding to 50 litres.

q: 266. The mixture which produces a steady stream of concrete as long as it is in operation is known as ........
explain: A continuous mixer is specifically designed to produce an uninterrupted, steady stream of mixed concrete for as long as it remains in operation.

q: 267. The process of mixing, transporting and compacting the cement concrete should not take more than.
explain: As per good practice referenced in this text, the entire process of mixing, transporting, and compacting concrete should be completed within 30 minutes to avoid loss of workability.

q: 268. For continuous transportation of concrete, the method used is
options: transport of concrete by wheel barrows
transport of concrete by belt conveyors
explain: Belt conveyors allow a continuous, uninterrupted flow of concrete from the mixing point to the placement location, unlike batch-type transport such as pans or wheel barrows.

q: 269. For concreting of tunnel lining, the concrete is transported by
explain: Pumping is the preferred method for transporting concrete into confined spaces such as tunnel linings, where access is restricted.

q: 270. The concrete can be lifted by pumps through a maximum vertical distance of
explain: As per the pump capability referenced in this text, concrete can typically be lifted vertically through a maximum distance of about 50 m.

q: 271. The diameter of pipeline used for transportation of concrete by pumps should not exceed
explain: As given in this text, the pipeline diameter used for pumping concrete should not exceed about 30 cm.

q: 272. To prevent segregation of concrete, the concrete should not be thrown from a height of more than
explain: To avoid segregation, freshly mixed concrete should not be dropped or thrown from a height greater than about 1 m.

q: 273. The process of consolidating concrete mix after placing it in position is termed as
explain: Compaction is the process of consolidating freshly placed concrete to expel entrapped air and achieve maximum density.

q: 274. When the concrete mix is too weighty, it causes
explain: An overly wet/heavy concrete mix can lead to segregation, effectively lower compacted density, and excess laitance rising to the surface — all of these can occur together.

q: 275. For compacting large section of mass concrete in structures, the type of vibrator used is
explain: For large mass concrete sections, an internal (immersion) vibrator is used, as it can be inserted directly into the thick concrete mass for effective compaction.

q: 276. For compacting plain concrete or one way reinforced concrete floors, the vibrator used is
explain: For thin, flat slabs such as one-way reinforced or plain concrete floors, a screed vibrator running along the surface is the appropriate compaction tool.

q: 277. The final operation of finishing the concrete surface is called
explain: Trowelling is the final surface finishing operation performed on concrete to achieve a smooth, hard, and dense top layer.

q: 278. The process of hardening the concrete mix by keeping its surface moist for a certain period is called
explain: Curing is defined as maintaining adequate moisture at the concrete surface for a specified period to allow proper hydration and hardening.

q: 279. Under normal circumstances, the beams soffits may be removed after
explain: Beam soffits (bottom formwork), which support the self-weight and construction loads of the beam, are typically kept in place longer, removed after about 14 days under normal conditions.

q: 280. Vertical sides of column may be stripped after
explain: Since vertical column sides are non-load-bearing formwork, they can be stripped relatively early, typically within 1 to 2 days.
